messages:
maya: Heads-up — after landing the prefix-cache changes in staging, we see a perf regression on common chat workload. P50 up ~12ms, P95 up ~85ms for short-turn dialogs. Repro steps: run 10k requests with prefix-heavy cache hit rate ~65%.
liam: Can you paste the profiler traces and the serving config used for the run?
andre: I grabbed a flame graph, looks like batching formation step is spending more time trying to pack with cache-awareness. Also kernel selector chooses a different matmul path for many requests due to shorter dynamic seqs. attaching small excerpt: 
```
# profiler excerpt
pack_time_ms: 18 -> 46
queue_wait_ms: 5 -> 7
kernel_select: cuBLAS->custom_fused for 64-token paths
KV-cache_hits: 65% -> 64% (no big change)
```
maya: full run metrics (staging): P50=42ms -> 54ms, P95=120ms -> 205ms, throughput 1.18k->1.05k req/s, token cost +6% 
rachel: Oof. Could be packing heuristic doing too much work per-request to decide cache-aware placements. We tuned packing to prefer same-prefix grouping (cache-hit coalescing) which may increase pack-search complexity. @liam any quick ideas? :thinking_face:
liam: Two axes: 1) limit search depth for cache-aware packing, 2) fall back to fast FIFO pack when queue latency crosses threshold. Also lower token_budget_target for packing so more smaller batches go out.
perf-bot: Aggregated before/after (10k reqs):
- avg_batch_size: 14.7 -> 12.1
- batch_formation_time_ms: 9.2 -> 31.8
- avg_tokens_per_batch: 228 -> 197
- cache_hit_grouping_ratio: 0.58 -> 0.73
ops-bot: deploy staging job #382 deployed prefix-cache-2026-03-12 at revision d7a2c0
andre: Kernel selection note: when cached prefixes reduce active KV-length, some requests fall into shorter-len kernel path which is faster per-token but also creates more variance in per-request runtime; combined with smaller batches we now see higher tail latency. The selector is doing the right thing but the batching layer must adapt token_budget_target and queue_policy.
liam: Proposed quick config tweak to test (staging canary):
```
# cache-aware packing quick-tune
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  token_budget_target: 1024  # lower than previous 1536
  max_batch_size: 32
  cache_aware_packing:
    enabled: true
    search_depth: 3        # cap how many candidate batches to evaluate
    grouping_bonus: 0.25   # prefer same-prefix packs but not too strongly
queue_policy:
  fallback_on_slo_ms: 120  # if queue_wait causes P95 > 120ms, use fifo
  priority: [cache_hits, age]
```
rachel: +1 to search_depth cap. Also try increasing the async dispatch horizon so we don't block on finding best pack (i.e., send suboptimal pack if wait > X ms).
maya: Ran a canary with liam's tune: batch_formation_time_ms dropped to 12ms, avg_batch_size 13.4, P95 down to 145ms (better but not fully recovered). Throughput 1.12k req/s. Cache grouping ratio 0.68.
andre: Nice. We should also tweak kernel_selector thresholds: add hysteresis so small changes in seq-length don't flip kernels for in-flight batches. That will reduce variance.
liam: Quick kernel selector patch idea: require delta_seq_len_pct > 15% to switch kernel; otherwise stick to current selection for batch. Can be toggled per-model.
perf-bot: Canary #7 stats vs baseline: P50 -2ms, P95 -60ms, throughput +3%, cost_per_token -1.2%
maya: Good signal. Plan: promote tune to staging for 24h, run full eval with diverse prefix distributions (0%, 25%, 50%, 75% cache-hit mixes). If stable, roll to prod with controlled ramp.
rachel: Also add instrumentation: histogram of pack-search iterations per request and kernel_switch_count per batch. That will help detect re-flip hotspots.
andre: FYI one regression surfaced earlier — the cache eviction policy changed LFU->LRU in the earlier PR which temporarily reduced cache hit locality; rolled back. Confirmed not the cause here.
liam: Action items: 
- maya: run 24h staging run with new tune + logs (pack-search histograms)
- andre: submit kernel_selector hysteresis patch (small perf test)
- rachel: add alert if avg_pack_time_ms > 25ms or pack_search_iters median > 4
- ops: schedule small canary rollout to 2% if staging looks good
maya: sounds good. I'll post a follow-up thread with the 24h summary. Thanks all :rocket:
